methodological_rigor.justification: Two-institution (DFBWCC, MGHCC) prospective observational cohort of 84 MIBC patients undergoing TMT with serial Signatera tumor-informed ctDNA monitoring. Paired pre/post-CRT samples available in 46 patients. Analyses include Fisher exact test for clinical stage vs ctDNA detection, Kaplan-Meier with log-rank test for MFS, and descriptive comparisons by recurrence type. Sample size is adequate for primary associations but limited for subgroup analyses (e.g., 5 isolated MIBC recurrences, 7 NMIBC recurrences). Median follow-up is short (11.3 months, range 0.4-40), limiting long-term outcome inference. No multivariable adjustment for clinical covariates.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Prospective consented observational cohort study at two academic centers - Oxford LoE 2b. Clinical relevance is high because TMT is an increasingly used bladder-sparing approach with unclear ctDNA biomarker utility until now. Findings directly inform design of correlative studies in ongoing phase III trials (SWOG/NRG 1806, KEYNOTE-992) and potentially support ctDNA-guided metastatic surveillance after TMT.

reporting_quality.justification: Ethics compliance explicitly referenced (Declaration of Helsinki, institutional review board-approved protocol with written consent). Cohort characteristics, inclusion, ctDNA assay details (Signatera, 16-variant bespoke assay, whole-exome sequencing-based) all documented. Use of commercial assay rather than research-grade is a transparent limitation. Software tools (SankeyMATIC, Prism) disclosed. Supplementary tables reference additional data. STROBE adherence is appropriate though not explicitly stated. Data availability beyond supplementary files not discussed.

novelty_literature.justification: First large multi-institutional cohort specifically characterizing ctDNA dynamics and recurrence patterns in MIBC patients treated with TMT (bladder-sparing therapy). Extends ctDNA literature from the radical cystectomy setting (IMvigor011, Christensen et al., Nordentoft et al.) to the TMT context. Novel clinical insight: ctDNA detects metastatic but not local (MIBC or NMIBC) recurrence - an important distinction for surveillance strategy design. Explicitly positions urine cfDNA as the complementary approach for local recurrence detection.

writing_presentation.justification: Concise and well-organized manuscript with clear sections, appropriate use of Sankey diagram and Kaplan-Meier plots, and focused clinical messaging. Limitations transparently acknowledged (cohort heterogeneity, variable ctDNA testing cadence, short median follow-up). Discussion effectively contextualizes findings relative to RC ctDNA literature and upcoming phase III TMT trials.

key_strengths: First multi-institutional cohort (n=84) specifically characterizing ctDNA dynamics in MIBC patients treated with trimodality therapy, addressing an explicit literature gap
Clear clinical differentiation: ctDNA detectability strongly correlates with metastatic recurrence (P < 0.0001) but not with isolated local (MIBC or NMIBC) bladder recurrence
Tumor-informed personalized Signatera assay with 16 variants per patient provides high-specificity monitoring
ctDNA conversion preceded clinical metastasis detection by median 8.3 weeks (range 0.6-24.9), suggesting potential utility as an early detection biomarker
Provides rationale for urine cfDNA as complementary modality for local recurrence detection
key_concerns: Median follow-up (11.3 months) is relatively short for definitive survival inferences in MIBC
Small event numbers in subgroup analyses: 5 isolated MIBC recurrences, 7 NMIBC recurrences, limiting statistical power
No multivariable adjustment for clinical covariates that might confound ctDNA-outcome associations
Heterogeneity in ctDNA testing cadence across the cohort acknowledged but not addressed analytically
Variable proportion of patients received neoadjuvant (19%) or adjuvant (14%) systemic therapy, potentially confounding ctDNA dynamics interpretation
chief_reviewer.rationale: Clinically important ctDNA biomarker study filling a specific gap for bladder-sparing MIBC management with clear differentiation of metastatic vs local recurrence surveillance utility, fitting Tier 2 (Clinical Cancer Research / ESMO Open-caliber) with minor revisions; short follow-up and small subgroups preclude higher tier.
